Elena —

Appreciate the concise ask. High-level response and proposed next steps below. We can assemble the SIG crosswalk and a scoped evidence packet and have it to you in two business days, with a recorded walkthrough the following week.

High-level answers:
- SIG crosswalk: we will deliver an RFI_Control_Crosswalk_NB_v1.xlsx with control-to-artifact mapping, ownership notes, and expected redaction level per artifact.
- Telemetry capture: Hosted API requests emit structured traces (OpenTelemetry spans) and request-level telemetry (request_id, model, latency_ms, region, response_size_tokens). Default sampling is adaptive (1% for low-volume customers, full traces for error-rate anomalies; configurable for enterprise customers).
- Audit logs: Admin and tenant-level admin events (user creation, key rotation, role change, model pinning) are logged to our immutable audit pipeline (retention 2 years by default for enterprise contracts). We can extract redacted samples.
- SIEM integration: We support push delivery to customer-managed S3 buckets (encrypted), a webhook-forwarder option, and a Fluent Bit / syslog forwarder for SIEM ingestion.
- Compliance artifacts: attached is our most recent SOC2 Type II summary and the crosswalk draft (see attachments). The full SOC2 report will be provided under NDA/controlled access.

Proposed immediate deliverables (timeline):
1) Within 48 hours: draft crosswalk (RFI_Control_Crosswalk_NB_v1.xlsx) + short artifact index.
2) Within 3 business days: redacted audit log sample and a short runbook describing telemetry exports.
3) Schedule a 45-minute walkthrough (options below).

Proposed walkthrough slots (PST):
- Wed 2027-10-06 10:00–10:45
- Wed 2027-10-06 15:00–15:45
- Thu 2027-10-07 09:30–10:15

If those don't work, send some times and we'll accommodate.

Subject: Re: RFI: Observability and telemetry for hosted deployment — technical clarifications

Elena — following up with technical clarifications to the items Jordan outlined. Short, actionable points you can include in your evaluation:

1) Tracing and spans
- We emit OpenTelemetry-compatible spans (OTLP over gRPC) for all request flows in the hosted API. Each span includes request_id, customer_id (hashed), route, backend_model, and end-to-end latency.
- Trace retention: full traces retained 30 days in hot storage, 12 months in warm storage, and archived up to 36 months on request for enterprise contracts.

2) Request logs / audit logs
- Admin/audit events are written to an append-only Kafka topic consumed by our compliance pipeline and exported to a WORM S3 bucket (server-side encrypted with CMKs).
- Redaction: PII fields are redacted at ingestion and we can provide a redacted sample (sample-audit-log.txt attached).

3) Export options and formats
- Parcel export: daily encrypted bundles to customer S3 (parquet + newline-delimited JSON for logs).
- Real-time forwarding: we provide a webhook sink and a Fluent Bit connector to stream to customer's syslog/SIEM.

4) Evidence access
- We provide a secure evidence portal (temporary signed URLs) under per-artifact ACLs and an audit trail of downloads. For SOC2 full reports we provision controlled access via our evidence portal and a short-term signed link.

If you require schema examples, we can include an OTLP span sample and the parquet schema in the packet.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
